summary: Phase 2 RealProfits eSign tested end-to-end: 17/17 Phase-1 regression PASSED, 14/15 Phase-2 backend tests PASSED, all 5 frontend flows PASSED. APScheduler boot log confirmed in backend.out.log. Only one backend bug: /api/billing/webhook returns 503 when STRIPE_API_KEY=sk_test_emergent because _stripe_key() is invoked at the top of the handler — defeats the whsec_test local-test idempotency path.

minor.issue: Handler calls _stripe_key() at the very top, which raises 503 STRIPE_KEYS_NEEDED whenever STRIPE_API_KEY=sk_test_emergent. This blocks idempotency testing and any local webhook simulation even though STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_test is meant to bypass signature verification. Fix: only call _stripe_key() inside the `if webhook_secret and webhook_secret != 'whsec_test'` branch (or defer the stripe.api_key assignment until the dispatch needs a Stripe API call). Currently the entire local-test webhook flow returns 503.

action_items: Fix billing webhook 503 trap: move _stripe_key() invocation inside the signed-only branch in /app/backend/billing/routes.py::stripe_webhook so local idempotency (whsec_test) works without real Stripe keys.
critical_code_review_comments: billing/routes.py: stripe_webhook eagerly calls _stripe_key() at entry — breaks the documented whsec_test bypass and prevents subscription_events idempotency from being exercised without real keys. Move the call after the JSON-parse branch.

billing/routes.py: Test-mode auto-creation of Stripe Product/Price (lines 82–91) is convenient but should be guarded behind an env flag or admin-only path to avoid surprise Stripe object creation in production.

billing/routes.py: portal endpoint returns 400 before 503 when no stripe_customer_id exists, which masks the 'Stripe not configured' state for users without a customer yet. Consider checking _stripe_key() first so the UX is consistent (got 503 in our test only because admin already had a customer_id from a previous run? — actually got 503, but order is fragile).

esign/routes.py line ~133: `branding_required or True` always evaluates True — works for free, but for paid tiers the intent (default True, user-overridable) is hidden. Replace with explicit boolean logic.
billing/saved_signature.py: 500KB limit is checked against the data-URL length (base64), not raw bytes; OK but document it.
seed_data_creation: Test docs TEST_TG_*, TEST_TooManySigners, TEST_Branding cleaned up via teardown. Reset subscriptions.docs_used_this_month to 0 at finish.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 2 scope: billing + scheduler + saved sig + verify landing. All scoped functionality works EXCEPT the webhook handler's premature _stripe_key() call. After fix, re-run `pytest tests/test_phase2_billing.py::TestWebhookIdempotency -v` — it expects a 200 on first POST and 200+duplicate=true on second POST with same event id. Reset docs counter with: su - postgres -c "psql -d realprofits_esign -c 'UPDATE subscriptions SET docs_used_this_month = 0;'" before tier-gating retests. Scheduler boot log confirmed: '[scheduler] Started: reminders (hourly), expire_docs (daily), reset_counters (monthly)' in /var/log/supervisor/backend.out.log.

rca of the issue: Webhook 503: stripe_webhook() at /app/backend/billing/routes.py line ~247 calls `stripe.api_key = _stripe_key()` before any branching. _stripe_key() raises HTTP 503 STRIPE_KEYS_NEEDED whenever STRIPE_API_KEY=='sk_test_emergent'. This short-circuits the JSON-parse + idempotency path that was designed to work in local-test mode (STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_test). Mitigation: only set stripe.api_key when actually calling Stripe SDK (e.g., inside _sync_subscription or signature-verification branch). Reproduction: POST /api/billing/webhook with body '{"id":"evt_x","type":"customer.subscription.updated","data":{"object":{"customer":"cus_nope","id":"sub_x"}}}' and Content-Type application/json — currently returns 503; should return 200 + log SubscriptionEvent row.
